ud7.10:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.
ud7.10:1.3: Then at that time when King Udena had gone to the pleasure park, the inner quarters (of the palace) were burnt down, and five hundred women died with (Queen) Sāmāvatī at their head.
ud7.10:2.1: Then many monks, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up their bowls and robes, entered Kosambī for alms,
ud7.10:2.2: and after walking for alms in Kosambī, while returning from the alms-round after the meal, went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.
ud7.10:2.3: While sat on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:
ud7.10:2.4: “Here, reverend Sir, when King Udena had gone to the pleasure park, the inner quarters (of the palace) were burnt down, and five hundred women died with (Queen) Sāmāvatī at their head.
ud7.10:2.5: What is the destination of the female lay followers, reverend Sir, what is their future state?”
ud7.10:3.1: “There are in this female lay followers who are stream-enterers, monks, there are once-returners, there are non-returners
ud7.10:3.2: - none of those female lay followers died, monks, without (having attained some) result.”
ud7.10:4.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud7.10:5.1: “The world, in bondage to delusion, ~ is looked on as being beautiful,
ud7.10:5.3: The fool, in bondage to cleaving, ~ is surrounded by darkness.
ud7.10:5.5: It seems like it is eternal,
ud7.10:5.6: ~ (but) there is nothing (to hold to) for the one who sees.”
